newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads - Giving up some ground.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads - Giving up some ground.

text.p: The Australian bond market gave up some ground against the dollar bloc after its recent strong outperformance, most notably against Canadian debt.

A rebound in the Canadian dollar on Monday from a two-year low against the U.S. dollar helped to underpin the debt market there, although differentials still remain well below levels seen prior the Federal Reserve rate hike on March 25.

The Canadian market has been under pressure on the expectations the Bank of Canada will have to follow the Fed, particularly if the Fed moves again in May, which the recent U.S. data flow seems to suggest, analysts said.

This has prompted some switching to the Australian market in recent days, which helped it to outshine U.S. Treasuries with the Australian/U.S. 10-year spread having narrowed to its lowest level since mid-February.

The local market maintained a reasonably positive tone after today's well received A$600 million Treasury bond tender, which could see the market renew its outperforming trend once the supply is fully digested and Thursday's labour force report is out of the way, analysts said.
"If...the employment data are weak, as we suspect, the spread could tighten to 100 basis points this week," said Su-Lin Ong, fixed income economist at Hambros Bank.
"A neutral decision on the living wage claim and favourable inflation data later this month should keep the spread tight in a range of 100-120 bp," Ong added.
But she felt there would be pressure for this spread to widen again over the medium term on evidence of stronger growth.
There was still no firm news on when the living wage claim verdict will be made.
